learning_outcomes.text: The student is able to characterize different trends occurring in the evolution of organization and management theory, and to describe the most important concepts of both traditional and modern management.
The student is able to characterize basic mechanisms of organization, to distinguish between types of organizational structures, to list components of the organization and its environment.
The student is able to describe how to implement various functions in the organization and management style.

syllabus_topics: The management process. Manager, managing at different levels and areas of the organization.
The environmental context of management. Planning and decision making.
teaching_methods: Traditional lecture with the use of transparencies and slides.
assessment_rules: The final grade (P) is based on the forming evaluation (F1), which is a test covering PEK_W01, PEK_W02, PEK_W03.
bibliography: Griffin R.W., Management. 11th Edition, South-Western Cengage Learning 2013
Coulter M., Robbins S.P., DeCenzo D., Fundamentals of Management. Global Edition. 8th Edition, Pearson, 2013
DuBrin A.J., Essentials Of Management. 9th Edition, South-Western Cengage Learning, 2012
Kinicki A., Williams B.K., Management. A practical introduction. 5th Edition, McGraw-Hill, 2010
McKee A., Management. A Focus On Leaders, Prentice Hall, 2012
Hatch M.J., Cunliffe A.L., Organization Theory. Modern, Symbolic, And Postmodern Perspectives, Oxford University Press, 2013
degree: Mechanical Engineering and Machine Building (I level, full-time)
